plain_text:
Holyoke Commission on Disabilities
Meeting Minutes 
Thursday, August 27, 2026 at 5:30pm
This meeting was held in-person and virtually via Zoom and telephone access in accordance
with current Massachusetts Open Law (OML) guidelines for remote access as extended by
Governor Healey from March 2025 to June 2027.  The host for this meeting was Kelly Curran.  
Members in attendance were:  Chairperson and Treasurer Jessica Lebron-Martinez and City of
Holyoke ADA Compliance Officer Kelly Curran
Members attending virtually: Secretary Elizabeth "Betty" Larivee, Marlene Connor, and Sarah
Wedaman
Absent:  Liana Pasialis (there has been no contact from her regarding membership)
Others attending meeting:  Kenneth Hohenburger (in attendance) and Lyn Horan (virtually)
Documents used in this meeting:
Meeting Agenda with information for Zoom and phone access
Draft Minutes of the Commission Meeting dated June 25, 2026
Letter regarding complaint on accessibility at entrance to Wyckoff Country Club's parking and
ballroom
Handicap Parking Applications at 240 Walnut Street and 340 Maple Street
Email from Mayor Garcia regarding events on 8/29 and 9/11/26
Technical difficulties with audio feedback delayed the start of this meeting. At 5:37pm,
Chairperson Jessica stated that this meeting was being recorded and officially called the
meeting to order. She then completed a roll call for attendance. Present at this time: Kelly,
Jessica, Betty, Marlene, and Sarah, 
Public Comment:  
Mr. Hohenberger spoke about his concerns regarding the rear entrance to City Hall which is the
handicap accessible doorway.  He stated that the uneven surfaces from the parking lot to
inside the building are a disaster. He also mentioned that the end of Race Street is not slated
for renovation like the other sections of Race Street but it is in deplorable condition so disabled
individuals have extreme difficulty entering any business in that area.  Both of these areas need
to be renovated and brought up to current standards.
Kelly Curran mentioned that the parking deck behind City Hall will be torn down and renovated
around the end of this year so the doorway issue will be addressed at that time.
Lyn Horan spoke about the accessibility of City Hall.  She said the basement level accessible
bathroom is locked at night and not available when meetings are occurring at City Hall.  The
bathroom behind the Council Chambers, which is used during meetings, is not accessible. This
situation needs to be addressed and corrected. 
Lyn gave the Commission "congrats" on getting the Citizen's Survey out to the public at various
events.  She also spoke briefly about the pending handicap parking applications.
Holyoke Commission on Disability Meeting Minutes for August 27, 2026                 page 2 of 3
Approval of Meeting Minutes:  
Minutes from the meeting of June 25, 2026 were previously e-mailed to members. Marlene
made a motion to approve the minutes; seconded by Sarah.  No corrections or edits were
offered; no discussion occurred.  Roll call vote was unanimous approval from Betty, Sarah,
Marlene, and Jessica.
OLD BUSINESS:  Jessica reviewed items that were discussed in the Commission's last
meeting:
Election of Officers:   position of Vice-Chair is still unfilled
Budget Funding FY'26:    This budget was closed as of June 30th.
Budget Funding FY'27:   The City Council passed our budget request for $36,000 and the
Mayor has approved that amount. 
Accessibility Survey:  Kelly reported that 30 responses had been received as of last week.  The
Survey was recently sent to all City Department Heads for distribution.  She has lots of printed
copies ready for distribution.  Jessica asked about setting up tables to continue distributing the
Surveys at upcoming events - Kelly said it is possible because the Commission has a budget
item for expenses to buy needed supplies and associated fees. Sarah asked to have the
Survey sent to her as a physical link - not QR Code.  Kelly immediately sent it to all
Commission members.
22G Fund Account:   No updates from last month's discussion
Mass Wheelchair Repair Bills:  No updates from last month's discussion
Winter Parking Issues: Public Safety Committee and Ordinance Committee have recently
discussed this topic.  Further discussions will be held with the DPW.
NEW BUSINESS:
A complaint was filed by Linda Dupont of Chicopee regarding the Wycoff Country Club's
accessibility to their ballroom via the parking area, ramp to the doorway, and hand grip to open
the door.  The Holyoke Building Commissioner investigated the matter and found that the
business owner (Mr. Cesar Ruiz) is responsible for an exterior egress certification to be
performed by an independent contractor.  No further information has been received.
Handicap Parking Application:  Betty reported the following:
Parking Application was submitted for 240 Walnut Street.  This property has a side lawn used
for off street parking which is muddy and rutted during bad weather.  The homeowner has MS
and difficulty walking.  An on-street parking spot is needed for safety and mobility concerns.
Sarah made a motion to approve the application; seconded 
Holyoke Commission on Disability Meeting Minutes for August 27, 2026                 page 3 of 3
by Marlene.  Roll call vote was unanimous approval from Betty, Marlene, Sarah, and Jessica.
Parking Application was submitted for 340 Maple Street.  These condos do not have driveways
so on-street parking is used by everyone.  No information was included on a disability so the
Commission decided to hold this application for further information.
Other matters:
Holyoke Pride event was attended by Jessica, Kelly, and Lyn.  Surveys were distributed.
Kelly received contact information from Tyrone Bowie of Radio Show 103.5 FM for possible
discussion about the work of this Commission.
Marlene stated that she will be at the Senior Center the mornings of September 8th and 10th to
discuss the Commission and hand out the Surveys.  Jess plans to join her on the 10th.
MOD offers COD office hours via Zoom every third Wednesday of the month for those
interested in getting further information or anyone having questions to be addressed.
Request to remove a handicap parking sign at 107 Brown Ave was received by the City Council
on 8/4/2026 and sent to the Ordinance Committee.
On 8/13/2026, the Ordinance Committee dealt with various handicap parking applications.  All
applications had been reviewed by this Commission.  The Ordinance Committee denied
approval for all the applications:
76 Maple Street - applicant needs to deal with building management to obtain a handicap spot
in the parking lot behind the building.
216 Appleton Street - no on street parking is allowed in this area due to the two bridges and
on-going repair work.
91 No. East Street - this is a police parking enforcement matter, not a need for handicap
parking
186 Pine Street - applicant has a temporary disability, not permanent, so she does not meet the
qualifications for a permanent parking spot.
122 Leary Drive - this is a private development, not a public street 
14-16 School Street - per City Engineer, moving the handicap parking sign would interfere with
other signs already posted in this area.
Having no further business, Jessica thanked everyone for their participation in tonight's meeting
   Marlene made a motion to adjourn the meeting; seconded by Sarah.  Voice vote was
unanimous approval. The meeting ended at 6:35 pm.
The remaining Commission meetings have been scheduled on September 24th, October 22nd,
and December 10th.
Minutes approved at meeting of September 24, 2026
